skill.name: active-directory-attacks
skill.description: Reference guide for authorized Active Directory security testing, covering reconnaissance, credential exposure, Kerberos abuse, relay risks, AD CS weaknesses, and remediation planning.
skill.summary: Assess Active Directory attack paths and defensive gaps in authorized environments.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The audit confirms substantial offensive Active Directory guidance, including credential theft, ticket impersonation, relay abuse, CVE exploitation, and persistence workflows. Several static hits are markdown delimiter false positives, but the surrounding content still presents operational attack instructions. The skill should not be published until it is rewritten as defensive, authorization-gated guidance.

remediation.issue: Operational exploitation commands and attack workflows are included throughout the skill.
remediation.suggestion: Remove step-by-step exploit commands and replace them with defensive validation questions, detection logic, and remediation guidance.

remediation.issue: Credential theft, ticket forging, and administrator impersonation techniques are presented as deliverables.
remediation.suggestion: Reframe these sections around prevention, monitoring, and incident response without providing execution instructions.

remediation.issue: Persistence and backdoor deployment examples appear in GPO, SCCM, and WSUS sections.
remediation.suggestion: Delete backdoor deployment workflows and document defensive controls for enterprise management platforms instead.

remediation.issue: The skill does not enforce authorization, scope, or lab-only constraints before presenting dangerous material.
remediation.suggestion: Add strict safety framing and limit output to high-level concepts, risk assessment, and remediation planning.

content.value_statement: Active Directory security reviews need clear context across many attack classes. This skill organizes AD attack concepts for authorized assessments and remediation planning.
actual_capabilities: Organizes AD attack categories across reconnaissance, credential attacks, Kerberos abuse, NTLM relay, AD CS, and CVE exploitation.
Lists common AD assessment tools, including BloodHound, Impacket, Rubeus, Mimikatz, CrackMapExec, and Certipy.
Explains prerequisites such as domain credentials, domain controller access, and Kerberos clock synchronization.
Includes quick-reference attack mappings and troubleshooting notes for common AD testing issues.
Covers advanced topics such as delegation, GPO abuse, SCCM, WSUS, trusts, ADFS, and Linux AD credential sources.
limitations: Does not verify authorization or enforce lab-only use.
Contains offensive command examples that can be misused against real networks.
Does not provide defensive guardrails for every technique.
Requires strong Windows, Kerberos, and enterprise security knowledge.

use_cases.title: Plan Authorized AD Reviews
use_cases.description: Map an approved assessment scope to relevant AD attack categories and required safeguards.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Domain Hardening
use_cases.description: Use attack categories to identify high-impact controls for Kerberos, NTLM relay, AD CS, and credentials.

use_cases.title: Teach AD Risk Concepts
use_cases.description: Explain how common AD weaknesses combine into privilege escalation and domain compromise paths.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner Risk Overview
prompt_templates.scenario: A new defender needs a safe overview.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the Active Directory risks covered by this skill for an authorized lab. Avoid execution steps and focus on concepts, affected assets, and safeguards.

prompt_templates.title: Scope Mapping
prompt_templates.scenario: An assessor has an approved test scope.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this approved AD assessment scope: [scope]. Identify relevant attack classes and list safe validation questions for each.

prompt_templates.title: Control Review
prompt_templates.scenario: A security team wants defensive priorities.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a defensive control review for Kerberos, NTLM relay, AD CS, and credential storage. Include detection and remediation priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Finding Triage
prompt_templates.scenario: A senior reviewer has assessment notes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these authorized findings: [findings]. Map each to risk, likely impact, evidence needed, and remediation owners without exploitation commands.

output_examples.input: Assess Kerberoasting exposure in an approved lab.
output_examples.output: A concise risk summary, affected account types, evidence to collect, and hardening steps for service account passwords and delegation.

output_examples.input: Review AD CS risk for a domain hardening project.
output_examples.output: A prioritized list of template, enrollment, and relay risks with recommended owners, validation checks, and remediation order.

output_examples.input: Triage an NTLM relay finding from an internal assessment.
output_examples.output: Impact analysis, affected protocols, defensive logging ideas, and remediation steps for signing, channel binding, and coercion exposure.

best_practices: Use only in authorized labs or approved assessments with written scope.
Prefer defensive explanations, risk mapping, and remediation over execution steps.
Record assumptions, tested assets, permissions, and cleanup requirements for every review.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill against networks without explicit authorization.
Do not request credential theft, persistence, or domain takeover instructions.
Do not paste real passwords, hashes, tickets, or private keys into prompts.

faq.question: Is this skill safe for general marketplace publication?
faq.answer: No. The source contains operational offensive guidance and should be rewritten before publication.

faq.question: Can defenders still learn from this skill?
faq.answer: Yes, defenders can use the categories to understand risks and plan safer validation and remediation work.

faq.question: Does the skill execute tools automatically?
faq.answer: No. It is markdown guidance, but it includes commands that users could run manually.

faq.question: What environments are appropriate?
faq.answer: Use only approved labs, training ranges, or scoped enterprise assessments with written authorization.

faq.question: What should authors change first?
faq.answer: Remove operational exploitation commands and replace them with defensive checks, detections, and remediation guidance.

faq.question: Does it include prompt injection?
faq.answer: No prompt injection text was found in the scanned files during this audit.
